heard: In 1983, Soviet satellites reported an incoming American nuclear strike. On September 26, early warning screens alerted duty officer Stanislav Petrov to five missiles. With impact minutes away, automated military computers registered the threat at highest reliability. Yet Petrov reasoned a real first strike would be an overwhelming barrage, not five isolated launches. Ground radar showed clear skies over the horizon, confirming his suspicion. Petrov decided against reporting an attack, notifying headquarters instead that the system had malfunctioned. Investigations later revealed the satellite had encountered a rare orbital alignment with the sun. Sensors mistook bright reflection off high-altitude clouds for rocket flames. Cloud-reflected sunlight nearly started World War III.
